text: 🇲🇽⚖️ "It's not that cash is going to be prohibited — far from it." "…but rather to make it easier to use technology for digital payments. If you pay with CoDi, there are no commissions." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, on the Digital Economy Law The new law pushes CoDi, Banxico's QR payment system on SPEI: three taps from any bank app, and by law no commission for buyer or seller. Simplified N2 Bis accounts can be opened remotely without SAT registration, with the limit raised from 25,000 to 135,000 pesos. Goal: 50% digital-payment adoption by 2027. Cash will be phased down gradually only at gas stations and toll booths.

🇲🇽🏭 LEGO invests $400 million in Nuevo León — 1,300 new jobs. "Currently we buy more than 90% locally… Today in Mexico we have the largest plant in the world." — Nancy Sánchez Moya, LEGO Senior VP of Manufacturing for the Americas The 8.6-billion-peso expansion — a new packaging building and an automated warehouse, over 60,000 m² — runs 2026–2029, and LEGO expects to grow its Mexican supplier base by about 30%. Economy Secretary Marcelo Ebrard said foreign direct investment reached about $35 billion in the first half of 2026, with $14 billion more already announced and up to $20 billion expected by year-end.

🇲🇽🔍 "That is false, because there is a Mexican State." — President Claudia Sheinbaum Asked about Trump's UN claim that Mexico must "regain control of its own soil," Sheinbaum recounted her answer when a visiting U.S. security secretary told her cabinet the cartels were "out of control." Intentional homicides are down 50%: "If there were any link with any criminal group, we would not have the results we have. It would be impossible." On U.S. campaigns using Mexico: "Better look at the problems of the United States, and we look at the problems of Mexico."

🇲🇽🌎 "There must not be trade blockades, because they affect the peoples, not the governments." — President Claudia Sheinbaum Asked about the clash at the UN between the multilateralism defended by Guterres and Lula and a U.S. vision boasting of the kidnapping of President Maduro, Sheinbaum laid out Mexico's constitutional position — equality of states, self-determination, peaceful settlement of disputes through the UN — naming Palestine, the war in Iran, Venezuela and Cuba. A deep UN reform "would be very good," she said.

🚨🇲🇽 "I could say: 'It is very hard to live next to a country with such a high level of illicit drug consumption'... But I'm not going to say it." — President Claudia Sheinbaum At the UN General Assembly, Trump called Mexico the "epicenter" of the drug cartels, then said he has a good relationship with Mexico and that it is also fighting the cartels. Sheinbaum: "They take one part of the statement and then they don't take the other." She named what she could say about the U.S. — drug consumption, arms production — and left it there.
banner: "BUT I'M NOT GOING TO SAY IT"

text: 🔥🇲🇽 Zedillo: 9 years at the central bank, a pension of ~1.79 million pesos a year. "Zedillo worked only 9 years at the Bank of Mexico, only 9 years, and has an annual pension of close to 1 million 790 thousand." — President Claudia Sheinbaum Former Banxico governor Guillermo Ortiz, 11 years at the bank, gets about 300,000 pesos a month. López Obrador's ISSSTE pension is under 30,000 pesos a month; Sheinbaum estimates hers will be about 35,000.

🇲🇽🌎 "There must be no foreign interference in any election of any country." — President Claudia Sheinbaum Asked about reports of U.S. interference ahead of Brazil's October 4 election, Sheinbaum called Lula "a very good president" who restored zero hunger in just over a year, and cited Mexico's constitutional principle of self-determination: "In Brazil, let Brazilians decide freely. And whatever the people decide, let it be respected."

🇲🇽🏭 Mexico's new passenger trains: 70% national content required. "In the case of the trains themselves, they were tendered with a percentage of national content... 70 percent." — President Claudia Sheinbaum China's CRRC builds the Mexico City–Pachuca electric trains at the plant it opened in Mexico at the government's request. Alstom builds the 47 northern trains in Ciudad Sahagún, Hidalgo. Army engineers make the railway sleepers in their own plants. Only the rails are still imported — Mexican steelmakers chose not to make them.
